headline: Tanzid Hasan scores century in Australia, completing a historic milestone
summary: From Aminul Islam's first century in 2000 to Tanzid Hasan's feat in Darwin, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in every Test-playing nation.
details: Tanzid Hasan's century in Darwin, Australia, marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket. With this achievement, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in every Test-playing nation.
The journey began in November 2000 in Dhaka, where Aminul Islam scored the first-ever Test century for Bangladesh in their debut Test match.
Following Aminul, Mohammad Ashraful scored the first century away from home in 2001 in Sri Lanka, which remains the record for the youngest Test century maker.
Habibul Bashar followed in 2003 in Pakistan and 2004 in the West Indies, becoming the first Bangladeshi batsman to score centuries on two different continents.
In 2010, the team saw milestones in New Zealand (Mahmudullah) and England (Tamim Iqbal), with Tamim's century at Lord's being a legendary moment in Bangladesh cricket history.
Mushfiqur Rahim's century in Hyderabad, India, in 2017 was widely regarded as one of the best away innings for the country.
It took until 2021 for Bangladesh to score their first Test century in Zimbabwe, achieved by Mahmudullah, alongside centuries by Sadman Islam and Nazmul Hossain.
Mahmudul Hasan Joy's century in Durban, 2022, seorang as the only Bangladeshi to score a Test century in South Africa.
Tanzid Hasan's 2026 century in Australia completes the circle, achieving a feat in one of the world's toughest batting conditions.
While Bangladesh has not yet played matches against Afghanistan and Ireland, they have scored centuries in the following Test-playing nations they have played against.
caption:
From Dhaka 2000 to Darwin 2026: Bangladesh has finally scored Test centuries in every nation they've played!

Tanzid Hasan's century in Darwin, Australia, marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket. With this achievement, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in every Test-playing nation.

The journey began in November 2000 in Dhaka, where Aminul Islam scored the first-ever Test century for Bangladesh in their debut Test match.

Following Aminul, Mohammad Ashraful scored the first century away from home in 2001 in Sri Lanka, which remains the record for the youngest Test century maker.

Habibul Bashar followed in 2003 in Pakistan and 2004 in the West Indies, becoming the first Bangladeshi batsman to score centuries on two different continents.

In 2010, the team saw milestones in New Zealand (Mahmudullah) and England (Tamim Iqbal), with Tamim's century at Lord's being a legendary moment in Bangladesh cricket history.

Mushfiqur Rahim's century in Hyderabad, India, in 2017 was widely regarded as one of the best away innings for the country.

It took until 2021 for Bangladesh to score their first Test century in Zimbabwe, achieved by Mahmudullah, alongside centuries by Sadman Islam and Nazmul Hossain.

Mahmudul Hasan Joy's century in Durban, 2022, seorang as the only Bangladeshi to score a Test century in South Africa.

Tanzid Hasan's 2026 century in Australia completes the circle, achieving a feat in one of the world's toughest batting conditions.

While Bangladesh has not yet played matches against Afghanistan and Ireland, they have scored centuries in the following Test-playing nations they have played against.

headline_marked: Shafiqur Rahman [[urges special parliament session]] over energy crisis
headline: Shafiqur Rahman urges special parliament session over energy crisis
summary: The Leader of the Opposition and Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami has written to the Acting President seeking an urgent session to address power outages and economic instability.
details: Opposition Leader Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has written to Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed calling for a special session of the National Parliament to address the severe power and fuel crisis.
The letter, sent on Friday, was also copied to the Prime Minister and the Parliament Secretariat.
Dr. Rahman highlighted that uncontrolled load-shedding is making life miserable for ordinary citizens and causing severe damage to industrial production and business trade.
The letter further stated that the energy crisis has directly led to an increase in the prices of essential commodities and a deterioration of the overall law and order situation.
As a representative of the people, the Opposition Leader emphasized that they cannot remain silent during such a crisis and that meaningful discussion in Parliament is essential for a quick solution.
He urged the Acting President to immediately convene a special session to resolve the energy crisis and other associated national problems.
caption:
Uncontrolled load-shedding and rising prices: The Opposition Leader calls for an urgent parliamentary session to save the economy.

Opposition Leader Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has written to Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed calling for a special session of the National Parliament to address the severe power and fuel crisis.

The letter, sent on Friday, was also copied to the Prime Minister and the Parliament Secretariat.

Dr. Rahman highlighted that uncontrolled load-shedding is making life miserable for ordinary citizens and causing severe damage to industrial production and business trade.

The letter further stated that the energy crisis has directly led to an increase in the prices of essential commodities and a deterioration of the overall law and order situation.

As a representative of the people, the Opposition Leader emphasized that they cannot remain silent during such a crisis and that meaningful discussion in Parliament is essential for a quick solution.

He urged the Acting President to immediately convene a special session to resolve the energy crisis and other associated national problems.
